title: Reinforcing Singapore's Position as a Global Transport Hub
what_it_is: Reinforcing Singapore's Position as a Global Transport Hub

sections.label: Jebel Ali Port and Dubai Logistics Corridor
sections.summary: Jebel Ali Port, its free zone and Al Maktoum Airport form the Dubai Logistics Corridor, linking sea, land and air across 200 square kilometres and over 6,500 companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Jebel Ali Port, built in the 1970s to serve a modest emirate, became the gravitational centre that pulled in manufacturing, logistics, finance and tourism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: That maritime foundation then enabled something larger: today, Jebel Ali Port, its adjacent free zone, and Al Maktoum Airport together form the Dubai Logistics Corridor, linking sea, land and air across 200 square kilometres, connecting more than 6,500 companies with a 30-minute link between port and airport.

sections.label: Changi Airport opening and growth
sections.summary: The Government built Changi, which opened in 1981, handled 12.1 million passengers and close to 200,000 tonnes of air freight in its first year, and now connects over 170 cities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The Government built Changi, which opened in 1981 and in its first year handled 12.1 million passengers and close to 200,000 tonnes of air freight.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Today, it connects over 170 cities, anchoring Singapore's position as a logistics and business hub entirely disproportionate to our size.

sections.label: Singapore multimodal global connectivity strategy
sections.summary: The strategy for Singapore's long-term economic competitiveness is multimodal global connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The strategy for Singapore's long-term economic competitiveness is multimodal global connectivity.

sections.label: OCEANS-X and Maritime Digital Twin
sections.summary: OCEANS-X enables system-to-system connectivity with digital port clearance, while the Maritime Digital Twin combines port data with simulation tools for shared what-if testing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: OCEANS-X enables system-to-system connectivity between maritime companies and government agencies, with digital port clearance as an initial service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The Maritime Digital Twin combines real-time and historical port data with simulation and modelling tools, giving agencies, industry and researchers a shared environment to test what-if scenarios and de-risk decisions before they happen at sea.

sections.label: Model Governance Framework for Agentic AI
sections.summary: Singapore has introduced version 1.5 of the Model Governance Framework for Agentic AI, described as a world first and a strong start.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The good news is that Singapore has already introduced version 1.5 of the Model Governance Framework for Agentic AI, a world first and a strong start.

sections.label: MOT role at international bodies
sections.summary: MOT has served Singapore excellently, playing an influential role and negotiating favourable terms at the IMO under UNCLOS, at ICAO, and other platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: On this front, MOT has served Singapore excellently, playing an influential role and negotiating favourable terms at the International Maritime Organization (IMO), under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS); at International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), and other platforms.

sections.label: ASEAN connectivity and digital backbone
sections.summary: Singapore's ASEAN Chairmanship is asked to prioritise regional land, sea and air connectivity and to build an ASEAN digital backbone, data lake house and shared infrastructure layer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: As Singapore assumes the ASEAN Chairmanship next year, how will the Government ensure that land, sea and air connectivity within the region is a priority on the agenda?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Second, build an ASEAN digital backbone for transport, an ASEAN data lake house that allows verifiable data to be accessed securely and a shared regional infrastructure layer for cross-border, cross-domain orchestration and innovation.

sections.label: Tuas Port and Changi T5
sections.summary: Tuas Port and Changi Terminal 5 were designed with automation and data systems built in from the outset.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Tuas Port and Changi Terminal 5 (T5) are the clearest examples of this – both designed with automation and data systems built into the "concrete" from the outset.

sections.label: Alternative energy transport means
sections.summary: Since no legal agreement can fully guard against risks, alternative energy transport such as hydrogen in solid-state containers must be developed so resilience does not depend on a single physical link.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: No legal agreement can fully guard against those risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: We must therefore also develop alternative means of transporting energy, such as shipping energy in the form of hydrogen stored in solid-state containers so as to ensure our resilience is not dependent on a single physical link.

sections.label: Tuas Port automation and jobs
sections.summary: As Tuas Port scales up with automated cranes, AGVs and remote-controlled operations, PSA says the shift frees resources and creates higher-value jobs in remote operations, systems monitoring and control centre management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: As Tuas Port scales up with automated cranes, automated guided vehicles (AGVs) and remote-controlled operations, PSA has been explicit that this shift is meant to free up resources while creating more higher-value jobs for Singaporeans – in remote port operations, systems monitoring and control centre management, moving away from manual yard work.

sections.label: Insufficient technically trained workers
sections.summary: GPC Resource Panel feedback was that there are insufficient workers technically trained for the new technologies now being deployed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: One of the feedback from our GPC Resource Panel members was that there are insufficient workers technically trained for the new technologies now being deployed.

sections.label: Competency frameworks and career conversion
sections.summary: Feedback called for regularly refreshed competency frameworks and curriculum without slow approval processes, and the Government is asked to expand career conversion, transition and SkillsFuture programmes with updated specialised tracks for mid-career workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: A related feedback from our GPC Resource Panel was the need for competency frameworks and curriculum to be reviewed and refreshed regularly, and to do so without being weighed down by conventional approval processes that could take up to a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Much good work has already been done in manpower development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: But in light of these broader trends, I call on the Government to consider: Firstly, expand existing career conversion and transition programmes as well as other SkillsFuture programmes to include updated and specialised tracks that meet the demands of future transport so that mid-career workers get real support to transition.

sections.label: ASEAN cooperation, AI, workforce reskilling
sections.summary: Singapore must deepen ASEAN cooperation, build integrated infrastructure, invest in AI transport and governance, and reskill workers and youth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Singapore needs to deepen cooperation with ASEAN member states, learning from our partners' strength and complementing one another.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: We need to build stronger physically and digitally integrated infrastructure that can operate under unified systems and standards without compromising national sovereignty and security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: We need to increase investment in the application of AI in transport as well as AI governance research.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: At the same time, we must be vigilant and do not displace our people in pursuit of economic gain because at the end of the day, all these efforts are meant to improve the lives of our people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: We must therefore invest more in helping those already in the workforce to reskill or to pivot and be more deliberate in training our youth.

sections.label: Singapore Port 2025 throughput
sections.summary: In 2025, the Singapore Port handled 44.66 million TEUs and bunkering supplied over 56 million tonnes of marine fuel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In 2025, the Singapore Port handled 44.66 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) of container throughput while the bunkering sectors supplied over 56 million tonnes of marine fuel.

sections.label: Middle East conflict disrupts Hormuz shipping
sections.summary: Escalation after US-Iran hostilities in late February 2026 disrupted shipping and energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The severe escalation in the Middle East following the outbreak of hostilities between the US and Iran in late February 2026 has severely disrupted shipping and energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz and shattered hopes of global supply chain normalisation.

sections.label: Vessel bunching and maritime threats
sections.summary: Capacity crunch caused vessel bunching at Singapore, while vessels faced drone strikes, cyber threats, and high insurance premiums, including the Ever Lovely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to MOT, this capacity crunch led to severe vessel branching at the port of Singapore as container lines rapidly reshuffled schedules, omitted regional Middle Eastern port calls entirely and arrived at our berth in unpredictable, highly concentrated clusters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Commercial vessels navigating adjacent routes have faced direct kinetic threats from drone strikes alongside sophisticated cyber threats, like satellite spoofing and global navigation satellite system jamming, driving global maritime insurance premiums to punitive highs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This included a Singapore-registered ship, the Ever Lovely, on 25 June 2026.

sections.label: Sustainable aviation fuel levy postponed
sections.summary: Postponing the sustainable aviation fuel levy to January 2027 gives airlines flexibility while Singapore balances sustainability with Changi Airport's competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While the Government's decision to postpone the implementation of the sustainable aviation fuel levy to January 2027 provides airlines with greater flexibility in navigating a volatile operating environment, Singapore must continue balancing sustainably objectives with the need to preserve Changi Airport's competitiveness as a global aviation hub.

sections.label: Tuas Port foreign automated systems
sections.summary: Tuas Port's automated fleet and charging architectures rely on large-scale procurements from foreign engineering giants like Siasun and ABB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For example, while Tuas Port leads the world in automated fleet scale, its heavy autonomous vehicles and high-power charging architectures are built on large-scale procurements from foreign engineering giants, like Siasun and ABB.

sections.label: Risk of foreign technology adoption
sections.summary: Singapore risks becoming a low margin highway if it remains content as an exceptional adopter of foreign technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If Singapore remains content with being an exceptional adopter of foreign technology, we risk becoming a low margin highway.

sections.label: Maritime Innovation and Technology Fund
sections.summary: The Government has poured significant resources into these sectors through the Maritime Innovation and Technology Fund (MINT).

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Government has poured significant resources into these sectors through the Maritime Innovation and Technology Fund (MINT).

sections.label: Shift innovation funding to deep tech
sections.summary: One proposal is to shift innovation funding to deep tech software and intellectual property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: One, shift innovation funding to deep tech software and intellectual property.

sections.label: Mandate share data standards
sections.summary: Two, mandate share data standards via a national transport data trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Two, mandate share data standards via a national transport data trust.

sections.label: National transport data trust proposal
sections.summary: Singapore should explore a national transport data trust, following SGTraDex's demonstration of trusted data-sharing, and broaden global talent rotation to tech native tracks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Singapore successfully demonstrated how trusted data-sharing can work through the Singapore Trade Data Exchange (SGTraDex).

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We should therefore explore establishing a national transport data trust, a secure state-backed framework that enables participating operators to share anonymised operational data through common standards while safeguarding commercial sensibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Three, broaden global talent rotation to tech native tracks.

sections.label: Enhance maritime training and technology
sections.summary: MOT and MPA should enhance frameworks like the Tripartite Maritime Training Award and build automated systems so Singapore moves from technological adopter to platform creator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I call on MOT and MPA to significantly enhance our existing frameworks, such as the Tripartite Maritime Training Award.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We must boost retention incentives, enhance mid-career conversion pathways and work with Singapore firms to improve shipboard working conditions and mental health support, making these foundational tracks attract our youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Deep maritime technology is not about replacing our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: By building advanced automated systems, remote fleet management system, predictive maintenance systems and operating firms in Singapore, we can better enable our workforce to leverage their irreplaceable operational expertise from onshore command centres in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: By combining practical experience with advanced analytics, we can transform traditional operational careers in the highly productive technology-enabled professions, ensuring that more high-value decision-making and better paying jobs remain in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Today, the challenge is to master the digital and algorithmic architecture that commands our physical assets, like our ports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: We must move decisively from an efficient technological adopter to an aggressive platform creator, shifting from operational excellence to global technological leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: By capturing sovereign intellectual property, breaking data silos and building a tech-augmented local workforce, we can reinforce Singapore's position as the indispensable heart for maritime logistics for generations to come.

sections.label: Aviation and maritime sector contributions
sections.summary: Aviation contributes around 5% of GDP and employs over 60,000 people, while maritime handled a record 41.12 million TEUs with about 90% transshipped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our aviation sector contributes around 5% of Singapore’s gross domestic product (GDP) and directly employs more than 60,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our maritime sector is the world's largest container transshipment hub, handling a record 41.12 million TEUs last year, with around 90% of the containers transshipped through our ports.

sections.label: Maritime Digital Twin launch
sections.summary: MPA launched Singapore's first Maritime Digital Twin, a real-time virtual port model supporting planning, risk management and operational optimisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MPA has launched Singapore's first Maritime Digital Twin, a real-time virtual model of our port that supports planning, risk management and operational optimisation.

sections.label: AI transport job demand
sections.summary: As AI becomes embedded across the transport ecosystem, demand will grow for data analysts, systems engineers, cybersecurity specialists and digital operation managers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As AI becomes embedded across our transport ecosystem, demand will grow for data analysts, systems engineers, cybersecurity specialists and digital operation managers.

sections.label: Future intelligent transport hub vision
sections.summary: Singapore's future depends on combining technology, talent, trusted institutions and infrastructure to remain a leading, intelligent, trusted and innovative transport hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our future will not be determined simply by how many containers pass through our ports or how many passengers travel through our airports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It will be determined by whether Singapore becomes the place where technology, talent, trusted institutions and world-class infrastructure come together to create the transport ecosystem of the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we succeed, Singapore will remain not only a leading aviation and maritime hub, but also the world's most intelligent, trusted and innovative transport hub, creating better jobs for Singaporeans, strengthening our economic resilience and reinforcing our position at the heart of global trade.

sections.label: APEC digital infrastructure ranking
sections.summary: A 2024 APEC report ranked Singapore among the best for digital infrastructure and governance, but showed a dip in the people pillar.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: An Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) report published in 2024 ranked us among the best performing economies in terms of our overall digital infrastructure and digital governance frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, the same report shows a dip in Singapore's relative rank in the people pillar, defined as how well the economy's human capital leverages technology.

sections.label: Questions on platform progress and metrics
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to clarify progress on adoption and value creation metrics, universal usage, use beyond Singapore, and learning points from previous platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister thus clarify what progress have been made in terms of working towards the Government's declared adoption and value creation metrics, and to what universal usage of the system and also details of how this platform is used beyond our shores?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Additionally, what were the learning points taken on board from the previous attempts and attempted roll-outs of proceeding platforms?

sections.label: Shipping and Singapore GDP
sections.summary: Shipping, maritime, aviation and related industries account for around 12% of Singapore's GDP, and 90% of trade flows depend on sea lanes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: News reports and Government data suggest that shipping, maritime, aviation and related industries account for around 12% of Singapore's GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For Singapore's trade flows, which are about three times our GDP, 90% depends on sea lanes.

sections.label: Modern conflict and Singapore
sections.summary: Modern conflict includes attacks on critical infrastructure and grey zone tactics, and Singapore may bear costs even if not a direct party.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The expansion of modern conflict includes attacks on critical infrastructure, such as damage to submarine cables around the Baltics, Taiwan and the Red Sea, or the use of economic coercion and other grey zone tactics, whether these are blockades or disinformation campaigns, underscore how Singapore and Singaporeans may bear the brunt and costs of these apparently far away developments, even if we are not direct parties to the conflict.

sections.label: Risk frameworks and contingency plans
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify risk frameworks and contingency plans keeping Singapore connected if key supply routes are disrupted, and how agencies coordinate them.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify the specific risk frameworks and contingency plans that would keep Singapore connected if key maritime, aviation, digital or energy supply routes are disrupted and how these plans and frameworks are coordinated across agencies?

sections.label: Buffering Singapore's resilience
sections.summary: Singaporeans want to know how Singapore buffers itself, ensures food and essential supplies, strengthens transport and logistics resilience, and bakes contingency planning into economy and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even as we continue deepening our connections with the world, Singaporeans rightly want to know how we are buffering ourselves, how we ensure sufficiency of food and essential supplies, how we strengthen resilience in transport and logistics, and whether we have baked contingency planning into our economy and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Instead, ours is a story of constant adaptation, renewal and resolve.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We have to prove that our small open country can remain deeply connected to the world while retaining a fair, inclusive and ultimately resilient economy.

sections.label: Aviation industry and aerospace output
sections.summary: Aviation accounts for 5% of Singapore's GDP, T5 is under construction, SIA has 164 aircraft, and aerospace output exceeded $18 billion in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Today, the aviation industry accounts for 5% of Singapore's GDP, or around $30 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Planning and construction for T5 is currently underway to create future capacity to handle up to 114 million passengers per annum, and SIA currently has 164 aircraft in its fleet, with another 49 aircraft on its order books.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The aerospace maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) industry houses regional headquarters for more than 130 companies, including leading ones such as Airbus, Boeing, Rolls Royce, Pratt and Whitney, and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: And Singapore's aerospace output exceeded $18 billion in 2024 and accounts for about 10% of global MRO output.

sections.label: Autonomous solutions and aviation manpower
sections.summary: A new generation of autonomous solutions should be deployed in manpower-heavy roles, and CAAS launched the One Aviation Manpower Fund with about $200 million in government grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In the next decade or so, we should see a new generation of autonomous solutions deployed, particularly in traditionally manpower heavy roles, such as in-ground handling and facilities management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Also, the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) has launched the One Aviation Manpower Fund to attract and retain talents in the aviation sector, with some $200 million of government grant allocated.

sections.label: Hybrid-electric short-haul flights forecast
sections.summary: Battery improvements are estimated to make hybrid-electric short-haul flights within 1,000 nautical miles a reality in 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: With the rapid improvements in battery technology, it is estimated that in 15 years' time, hybrid-electric aircraft flights for short-haul flights within a range of 1,000 nautical miles will become a reality.

sections.label: Decarbonising short-haul flights
sections.summary: Short-haul flights emit four times more carbon per seat than long-haul, so switching them to fully electric flights should be prioritised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Short-haul flights create four times more carbon emissions per seat, compared to long-haul flights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Hence, decarbonisation of short-haul flights should be prioritised and switching them to fully electric flights will reduce overall aviation carbon emissions by an estimated 20%.

sections.label: Singapore international green air hub
sections.summary: Singapore could be a centre of excellence for hybrid-electric and electric aircraft R&D, with parts made in Johor and assembly in Changi East.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: To become an international green air hub, Singapore can be established as a centre of excellence for the R&D of hybrid-electric and electric aircraft, manufacture the aircraft parts in land abundant Johor, under our Special Economic Zone collaboration framework, assemble the aircraft back in Changi East Industrial Zone and finally, test flight the aircraft in Changi Airport.

sections.label: RIE2025 aviation R&D funding
sections.summary: Under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan, significant R&D funding has been set aside for the aviation sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan (RIE2025), significant R&D funding for aviation sector, for manufacturing, trade and connectivity purposes has been set aside.

sections.label: Aviation manufacturing high-paying jobs
sections.summary: Aviation manufacturing is high tech and high value, creating high-paying jobs using AI and 3D printing, as Nimbus Aviation's founders shared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: More importantly, aviation manufacturing is a high tech, high value industry and these new career pathways will create many high-paying jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: They can apply the latest AI and 3D printing technologies to design and build an electric aircraft from scratch.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Adrian Gooz and Akim Niyonzimas, the founders of Nimbus Aviation, shared that his team used AI and 3D printing to design and build its aircraft prototype, massively reducing the cost of R&D and the time required to commercialise a solution.

sections.label: Proposal for green air hub
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Minister for Transport will consider the proposal to create an international green air hub and grow the Centre of Excellence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: It is our time for an ambitious goal for air transport, from Paya Lebar to Changi almost 50 years ago, from fossil to green aviation today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister for Transport and his team will carefully consider my proposal to create an international green air hub and grow the Centre of Excellence for electric aircraft manufacturing in Singapore.

sections.label: Motion on world-class infrastructure
sections.summary: The Motion affirms that world-class infrastructure reinforces Singapore's position as a global transport hub and anchors good jobs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today's Motion affirms the role of a world-class infrastructure in reinforcing Singapore's position as a global transport hub and anchoring good jobs in, Singapore.

sections.label: North-South Corridor multimodal design
sections.summary: The North-South Corridor is designed to be multimodal with dedicated bus lanes and cycling paths so more Singaporeans, including non-car owners, can benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Non-car owning Singaporeans can only directly benefit from an eight-lane expressway if they are riding in a private hire car, or one of the bus services that ply an expressway sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is thus heartening that the upcoming of North-South Corridor is designed to be multimodal with dedicated bus lanes and cycling paths to allow as many ordinary Singaporeans, including those who do not own cars to directly use and benefit from the new expressway.

sections.label: London Freedom Pass eligibility
sections.summary: The Freedom Pass is given to London residents above age 66 and those with eligible disabilities to travel freely across the Transport for London network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Freedom Pass is given to London residents above the age of 66 and those with eligible disabilities to freely travel across the Transport for London network.

sections.label: Free travel and seniors' well-being
sections.summary: The Freedom Pass was described as providing access to essential goods and services and as a prized mechanism for participation in city life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Freedom Pass was described not only as providing access to essential goods and services but also as a widely prized mechanism for participation in life of the city." What the research suggests is that providing free travel on public transport helps with seniors' well-being and enables their civic participation.

sections.label: Merdeka Pass for senior citizens
sections.summary: As Singapore becomes a super-aged society, the speaker believes senior citizens here deserve their own Merdeka Pass.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As Singapore becomes a super-aged society, I believe that our senior citizens here similarly deserve their own Merdeka Pass.

sections.label: Self-driving bus pilots and night services
sections.summary: AVs have been trialled in Punggol, self-driving public bus services will be piloted in Marina Bay and One-North from the second half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: AVs have already been trialled in Punggol to ply short, fixed route services and self-driving public bus services will also be piloted in Marina Bay and One-North from the second half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Should the self-driving public bus service pilots in Marina Bay and One-North be successful, I would like to suggest that the Land Transport Authority (LTA) next consider deploying self-driving public buses to build a network of night bus services.

sections.label: Trialling self-driving buses overnight
sections.summary: The speaker urges LTA to consider trialling self-driving buses overnight, citing lower traffic and lower public safety risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And with AVs, what was previously economically and logistically infeasible could become a reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I urge LTA to seriously consider trialling self-driving buses on bus routes overnight as well, as this is a use case that could benefit many Singaporeans while traffic levels and any risk posed by the AVs to public safety are also much lower.

sections.label: Global robotaxi deployment numbers
sections.summary: Over 10,000 robotaxis are already deployed globally across the US, China, Europe and the Middle East.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Globally, over 10,000 robotaxis are already deployed across the US, China, Europe and the Middle East.

sections.label: Taxi fleet and PHC drivers
sections.summary: The taxi fleet has shrunk to about 12,000, while there are now over 60,000 PHC drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Today, the taxi fleet has shrunk to about 12,000, but we now have over 60,000 PHC drivers.

sections.label: Displaced drivers if AVs replace fleet

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: If AVs were to replace just 10% of this fleet, displacing 7,000 drivers, where will they go?

sections.label: Drop to 41% by 2025

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: By 2025, that number dropped to just 41%, a worrying 13% drop.

sections.label: Taxi and private-hire drivers' livelihoods
sections.summary: More than 70,000 taxi and private-hire drivers in Singapore earn their living ferrying passengers, supporting their families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In Singapore, more than 70,000 taxi and private-hire drivers brave the roads day in and day out to earn their living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For them, ferrying passengers is the safety net that keeps their entire families fed, housed, and clothed.

sections.label: Tripartite partners help drivers
sections.summary: The tripartite partners must start working together now to find alternative pathways for affected taxi and private-hire drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The tripartite partners must begin working together now to find alternative pathways for affected taxi and private-hire drivers.

sections.label: Disruption versus worker hardship
sections.summary: Disruption is inevitable, but hardship for workers is not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, disruption is inevitable, but hardship for our workers is not.

sections.label: NOL sold and dismantled
sections.summary: NOL was sold to France's CMA CGM in 2016, after its tanker fleet, headquarters and logistics arm were sold off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: NOL, the national carrier, was sold to France's CMA CGM in 2016, the last act in a long dismantling: the tanker fleet to Malaysia in 2003, the headquarters in 2012, the logistics arm in 2015 and then, the line itself.

sections.label: France and Korea shipping moves
sections.summary: France is putting 10 large ships under its flag via CMA CGM, while Korea rebuilt HMM after Hanjin collapsed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: France is putting 10 of the world's largest ships under its flag as a "strategic fleet" – requisitionable in a crisis, crewed by its own officers – using CMA CGM, the very company that bought our line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Korea, after Hanjin collapsed the same year we sold NOL, poured state billions into rebuilding Hyundai Merchant Marine (HMM) into a top 10 carrier through a dedicated sovereign vehicle.

sections.label: Few Singaporean officers on flag
sections.summary: Fewer than one in 12 officers on Singapore's own flag is Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fewer than one in 12 officers on our own flag is Singaporean.

sections.label: Gemini Network chose Tanjung Pelepas
sections.summary: The Maersk Hapag-Lloyd Gemini Network chose Tanjung Pelepas over Singapore as its most important hub in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While Singapore is still the world's largest transshipment hub, the Maersk Hapag-Lloyd Gemini Network still chose Tanjung Pelepas over Singapore as its most important hub in 2025.

sections.label: NOL sale strategic failure
sections.summary: The passage states one national carrier was kept and the other sold, calling it a big failure of strategic judgement that the Government should not have allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One set of hands kept one national carrier and sold the other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was a big failure of strategic judgement, and the Government should not have allowed Temasek to sell off NOL.

sections.label: Temasek holds PIL majority
sections.summary: Through Heliconia, Temasek holds the majority of PIL, the largest homegrown carrier, with 100-odd ships, profitable and strongest in Africa and the Global South.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Through Heliconia, Temasek holds the majority of PIL, our largest homegrown carrier, which has 100-odd ships, profitable and strongest where the giants are thin – in Africa and the Global South.

sections.label: Cost of doing it
sections.summary: The passage states that if it were done, it would cost billions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If we were to do it, it would cost us billions, too.

sections.label: France treats CMA CGM as sovereignty asset
sections.summary: France was the counterparty and treats CMA CGM, which bought NOL, as a sovereignty asset and is enlarging its national fleet while Singapore dismantled its own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: France was our counterparty and is a mirror.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It treats the company CMA CGM that bought our line NOL as a sovereignty asset and it is enlarging its national fleet, while we dismantled ours and called the matter settled.

sections.label: Rebuild shipping capacity after NOL
sections.summary: The passage asks what capacity Singapore can direct when shipping space is rationed, calls the NOL sale a very poor decision, and urges rebuilding shipping capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And three, when shipping space is next rationed, what capacity can Singapore actually direct?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: That the sale of NOL was a very poor decision, CMA CGM's ability to turn a net profit less than one year after acquisition clearly proves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My belief is that we must draw a line on Temasek's very poor decision to sell NOL in 2016, move on to rebuild our shipping capacity and make back the time we have lost.

sections.label: Framework linking trust to value
sections.summary: The passage proposes a framework where growing trust gives influence, influence creates integration, integration generates intelligence, and intelligence creates economic value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Today, I would like to propose a simple framework: growing trust to gives us influence; through influence, we create integration; integration generates intelligence; and intelligence creates economic value.

sections.label: Strengthening CAAS, MPA, Aviation Academy
sections.summary: Singapore should strengthen CAAS, MPA and the Singapore Aviation Academy as regulators and global platforms, and could pioneer an LLAMS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We should continue strengthening institutions, such as CAAS, MPA and the Singapore Aviation Academy, not only as regulators, but as global platforms for capability development, thought leadership and international collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I would also like to take this opportunity to acknowledge the outstanding work our CAAS officers, whose dedication helps Singapore secure re-election to the 36-member ICAO Council with the highest number of votes ever received by any member state in ICAO history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: For example, Singapore could pioneer an LLAMS, the digital operating system for low-altitude space.

sections.label: Multimodal gateway via T5 integration
sections.summary: Integrating T5 with Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal and regional links can create a multimodal gateway connecting the region to the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: By integrating T5 with Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal and stronger links to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, the oil and gas industry in Pengerang, the Batam-Bintan-Karimun (BBK) free trade zone and regional tourism destinations, we can create a truly multimodal gateway connecting this region to the world.

sections.label: AI, autonomous and quantum logistics
sections.summary: Singapore should build a National AI Logistics Control Tower, an autonomous logistics initiative, and a National Quantum Logistics Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: First, build the world's first National AI Logistics Control Tower, a digital brain for Singapore's logistics ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Second, make Singapore the world's living laboratory for autonomous logistics through the Singapore Autonomous Logistics Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Third, establish the world's first National Quantum Logistics Programme, combining AI and quantum optimisation to solve logistics challenges beyond the reach of conventional computing, from airline cargo allocation and multimodal routing to fleet deployment, port operations and supply chain resilience.

sections.label: Investing in transport workforce
sections.summary: The Ministry's continued investment in developing the transport workforce through initiatives such as OneAviation is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: And no operating system succeeds without great people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the Ministry's continued investment in developing our transport workforce through initiatives such as OneAviation which was launched by Minister of State Sun Xueling.

sections.label: Hub port structural vulnerability
sections.summary: A neutral hub port holds traffic only by staying competitive, as shown when Maersk and the Gemini cooperation shifted volume to PTP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As my hon friend and MP for Aljunied, Kenneth Tiong, pointed out earlier, a neutral hub port holds traffic only by staying competitive and a port cannot pick its carriers because carriers pick their ports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We saw the reality of this structural vulnerability when Maersk shifted its transshipment hub to the port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP) in the year 2000 and again in 2025, when the Gemini cooperation shifted the bulk of their joint shipping volume to PTP.

sections.label: Sovereign digital architect of trade
sections.summary: Singapore must pivot from being just a physical gatekeeper to also becoming the sovereign digital architect of global trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To hedge our exposure to physical trade volatility, Singapore must pivot from being just a physical gatekeeper to also becoming the sovereign digital architect of global trade.

sections.label: Redirecting concrete funds to software patents
sections.summary: A fixed percentage of spending on Changi T5 and Tuas berths could be redirected to acquiring supply chain software patents under Singapore's control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For every dollar spent on pouring physical concrete for Changi T5 or the Tuas berths, a fixed percentage could be redirected towards strategically acquiring, centralising and developing next-generation supply chain software patents under Singapore's sovereign control, such as automated customs clearing platforms and predictive route management networks.

sections.label: ILO algorithmic management report
sections.summary: A 2024 ILO and European Commission report gives empirical evidence on algorithmic management in transport and logistics workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 2024 report titled "Algorithmic Management Practices in Regular Workplaces – Case Studies in Logistics and Healthcare" by the International Labour Organization and the European Commission's joint research centre provides empirical evidence of what happens when algorithmic management is introduced in regular transport and logistics workspaces.

sections.label: Workplace Safety Act algorithm rules
sections.summary: Subsidiary Workplace Safety and Health Act regulations should require dispatch algorithms at critical transport hubs to factor in human physiological constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, we should update the subsidiary regulations in the Workplace Safety and Health Act to mandate that workforce management and dispatch algorithms used in critical transport hubs explicitly factor in human physiological constraints.

sections.label: Employment Act algorithmic transparency rights
sections.summary: Algorithmic transparency and explainability requirements under the Employment Act should give workers a statutory right to explanation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, we should introduce algorithmic transparency and explanability requirements under the Employment Act to give workers a statutory right to explanation.

sections.label: Sharing AI productivity gains
sections.summary: Operators achieving AI productivity breakthroughs should pass gains to workers as wage increases or shorter hours with no loss in base pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When transport logistics and aviation operators which achieve major productivity breakthrough through the use of AI, those productivity gains must be shared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Instead of squeezing headcount or expanding workloads, operators should be required to pass these gains down in the form of structured wage increases or compressed human-centric working hours with no loss in base pay.

sections.label: Aviation job redesign and logistics roles
sections.summary: Up to 30% of aviation jobs may be redesigned in five years, while logistics creates higher-paying PME roles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Up to 30% of aviation jobs may be redesigned within the next five years, mostly in ground handling, and more preparations are required as T5 is being constructed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In logistics, new, higher-paying roles will be created in professional, manager and executive (PME) jobs, including data analysis, supply chain management and software development.

sections.label: Platform worker injury rate
sections.summary: MOM's Workplace Safety and Health Report states platform workers had fatal and major injuries at 84.6 per 100,000 last year, nearly five times the whole workforce rate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM’s) Workplace Safety and Health Report, platform workers suffered fatal and major injuries at a rate of 84.6 per 100,000 last year – nearly five times higher than the rate for the workforce as a whole.

sections.label: Transport sector school-to-sector pathways
sections.summary: The question asks MOT how it intends to work through SWDA, the tripartite Jobs Council, NTUC and unions to develop clearer school-to-sector pathways into future transport sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask MOT on how it intends to work through the Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA), the tripartite Jobs Council, NTUC and our unions to develop clearer “school-to-sector" pathways into the future transport sectors, careers supported by internships, apprenticeships, structured traineeships and career guidance.

sections.label: Heat Stress Advisory and weather challenges
sections.summary: MSE and NEA launched a Heat Stress Advisory in 2023, and MSE works with agencies such as MPA and MOM to better manage weather-related challenges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For example, the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE), and the National Environment Agency launched a Heat Stress Advisory in 2023, while MSE is working with agencies, such as MPA and MOM, to better manage weather-related challenges.

sections.label: Bus driver accommodation at depot
sections.summary: SBS Transit recently opened Singapore's first dedicated accommodation for bus drivers at the Sengkang West Depot, with rooms, kitchens and a dedicated floor for women drivers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Recently, SBS Transit opened Singapore’s first dedicated accommodation for bus drivers at the Sengkang West Depot, with rooms, kitchens and even a dedicated floor for women drivers.

sections.label: Workers seizing new opportunities
sections.summary: It is about ensuring young and experienced workers can seize new opportunities, linked to the Economic Competitiveness Committee co-chaired with Mr Saktiandi Supaat.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is also about ensuring that our workers, both young and experienced, are able to seize the new opportunities that will emerge.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is closely linked to the work of the Economic Competitiveness Committee, which I co-chair with Mr Saktiandi Supaat.

sections.label: Better wages welfare work prospects
sections.summary: The passage states better wages, better welfare and better work prospects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Better wages, better welfare and better work prospects.

sections.label: Global trade contraction since crisis
sections.summary: International trade flows contracted sharply after the global crisis, with imports and exports in global output retreating since 2008.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since the gGlobal crisis, flows of international trade have contracted sharply, the drop was so severe in the immediate aftermath of the crisis that economists refer to this phenomenon as the Great Trade Collapse.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since 2008, the share of imports and exports in global output has gone into retreat, in stark contrast to the decades prior.

sections.label: Singapore downgraded to Tier 2
sections.summary: Singapore was degraded to Tier 2 status on suspicions its transshipment status was exploited to evade export controls.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore has not been spared, having been degraded to Tier 2 status on suspicions that our transshipment status had been exploited to evade export controls.

sections.label: Services trade and Singapore exports
sections.summary: Services trade shows no post-crisis slowdown and is one-fifth of global commerce, but Singapore's exports remain concentrated in goods.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Unlike merchandise trade services, have not demonstrated any post-global crisis slowdown and now accounts for one-fifth of global commerce.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But Singapore's export basket remains solidly more concentrated in the former, with goods accounting for about 110% of GDP versus 70% for services in terms of our exports.

sections.label: Improving market integration
sections.summary: Efforts should go to improving market integration through more services coverage in RCEP, CPTPP upgrades, and greater ASEAN market access.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Instead, we should devote our energies to improving market integration through introducing more services coverage to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, upgrading the agreement to include more high-level issues found in the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, and pushing for greater market access within ASEAN, especially when it comes to investment and non-tariff barriers.

sections.label: Caution in infrastructure planning
sections.summary: There may be a case to plan build-up in tranches and make parts of the blueprint contingent on future economic conditions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, there is wisdom in planning and building for the future.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But there may be a case to proceed with greater caution, perhaps by planning the build-up in tranches and making parts of the full blueprint contingent on whether future economic conditions justify the massive capacity expected.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, we might wish to structure the Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act (SINGA) bond borrowing in a manner that will only trigger if the project meets certain threshold conditions associated with anticipated need.

sections.label: Overseas stints for local talent
sections.summary: A more structured framework should encourage PMETs to spend a year or two in firms' affiliates in major ASEAN capitals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Where we have been less forward-facing, however, is in ensuring that our skilled local talent undertake stints abroad.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I believe that we should have a more structured framework for encouraging our PMETs to spend a year or two in their firms' affiliates or subsidiaries located in our major ASEAN capitals.

sections.label: Safeguards against big tech withdrawal
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Government, through the National AI Council, has a safeguard plan if big tech firms suddenly withdraw data centre access, AI models, platforms or APIs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even accepting that we may not build in-house foundational models from the ground-up, I would still like to know if this Government, through the National AI Council, has already developed a sort of safeguard plan in the event of sudden withdrawal by big tech firms to data centre access AI models, digital platforms or even application programming interfaces (APIs).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This may mean a very narrow set of options.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We may choose to hue to ideal principles ourselves – keeping tariffs at zero, maintaining the UNCLOS right of free passage or leaving capital actually on taxed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A practically minded Foreign Service and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) will have to leave room for occasionally departing from non-core principles.

sections.label: Adapting policy to future world
sections.summary: The Member says policy-makers should align policy with the likely world of tomorrow rather than bet on the ideal world of yesteryear.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is how I believe that our policy-makers should adapt.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We cannot bet on the ideal world of yesteryear but should instead align our policy with the likely world of tomorrow.

sections.label: Sitting suspended until 3.40 pm

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, I propose to take a break now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.40 pm.

sections.label: Workforce talent forecast and plans
sections.summary: The Member asks the Ministry for a forecast of talent needed, the local and foreign workforce mix, and plans to train, attract and retain workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share with us a forecast of the talent we will need – the expected mix of local and foreign workforce as well as the mix of key functions where demand is likely to grow?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: More importantly, what are our plans to train, attract and retain the workforce so that Singapore remains well-positioned for the next phase of growth?

sections.label: Energy security and Jurong Island refineries
sections.summary: The Member says Singapore must embrace sustainable technologies while keeping access to conventional fuels secure, reliable and diversified, and hopes the Government considers the future of the Jurong Island refineries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We must both embrace new, sustainable technologies, but also continue to ensure that our access to conventional fuels remains secure, reliable and diversified.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And so, I hope the Government will carefully consider the future of the Jurong Island refineries.

sections.label: Sustainable aviation fuel cost concerns
sections.summary: The Member says sustainable aviation fuel is estimated at two to four times jet fuel price, and mandating it and levies could make Singapore less attractive as an air transport hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The sustainable aviation fuel is still currently estimated to be about two to four times the price of jet fuel even when recent oil prices are at a record high due to the Middle East conflict.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The costs from mandating sustainable aviation fuel and the accompanying levies could make Singapore less attractive as an air transport hub, especially if neighbouring air hubs choose not to undertake similar measures.

sections.label: Chencharu new homes plan
sections.summary: Chencharu in Nee Soon South is planned to have about 10,000 new homes by 2040, bringing around 30,000 residents to the 70-hectare area.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Nee Soon South, Chencharu is planned to have about 10,000 new homes by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This means we can expect around 30,000 new residents to move into this 70-hectare area over the next 15 years, an average of 2,000 residents every year.

sections.label: Manpower and worker ratio forecasts
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to share projected manpower forecasts, the expected local to foreign worker ratio, and job functions likely to see growing demand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share with us the projected manpower forecasts, the expected ratio of local to foreign workers and the job functions likely to see growing demand?

sections.label: Commercial orders of $20 billion
sections.summary: Today, they have commercial orders of $20 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, they have commercial orders of $20 billion.

sections.label: Regional trial sites with neighbours
sections.summary: The passage asks whether regional trial sites with neighbouring countries can be explored, noting Malaysia's low altitude economy plan and proposed sandboxes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Should we or can we explore options of having such regional trial sites with the neighbouring countries?

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that Malaysia just announced its low altitude economy plan by the Transport Minister, by the Malaysia Prime Minister last week and that they are also proposing sandboxes.

sections.label: Integrated innovation agency proposal
sections.summary: The proposal is an integrated innovation agency under MOT with aggressive funding, piloting and regional collaboration for sandboxes and flight testing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will not suggest a sum, but I think such an endeavour needs strong support as it will allow us to create a new economy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, my proposal is an integrated innovation agency under MOT, with aggressive funding, aggressive piloting and collaboration within the region for sandboxes and flight testing.

sections.label: Tuas Port automated status
sections.summary: Tuas Port is becoming one of the world's largest automated ports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Tuas Port is becoming one of the world's largest automated ports.

sections.label: SME implementation support
sections.summary: Encourages continued efforts to strengthen hands-on implementation support for SMEs through trusted technology advisers, sector-specific consultancy and practical guidance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The last mile of digital transformation is implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I therefore encourage continued efforts to strengthen hands-on implementation support through trusted technology advisers, sector-specific consultancy and practical guidance that helps SMEs move from grant approval to successful execution.

sections.label: SME job redesign support
sections.summary: Calls for continued investment in SkillsFuture and workforce transformation, and exploring shared talent pools and collaborative programmes with partners such as Tech Talent Assembly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Job redesign, however, is especially challenging for SMEs, which often lack dedicated human resource and transformation teams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We should therefore continue investing in SkillsFuture and workforce transformation while exploring shared talent pools, industry attachments and collaborative innovation programmes with partners, such as Tech Talent Assembly, also an associate to NTUC, so that SMEs can access specialised expertise that would otherwise be beyond their reach.

sections.label: ASEAN Chairmanship 2027 priorities
sections.summary: As Singapore prepares to assume the ASEAN Chairmanship in 2027, it should deepen regional connectivity and champion common standards in digital trade, AI and interoperability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As Singapore prepares to assume the ASEAN Chairmanship in 2027, we should deepen regional connectivity and continue championing common standards in areas, such as digital trade, AI and interoperability.

sections.label: Hard-to-replicate national strengths
sections.summary: States that the institutional framework, credibility, professional talent and international reputation a country builds over the long term are truly difficult to replicate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What is truly difficult to replicate, however, is the institutional framework, credibility, professional talent and international reputation that a country builds over the long term.

sections.label: SME entering international supply chains
sections.summary: States that when a local SME enters an international supply chain through an innovative solution, the impact goes far beyond its own growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: When a local SME is able to enter an international supply chain through innovative solution, the impact goes far beyond its own growth.

sections.label: Singapore as trusted global hub
sections.summary: Says international partners trust Singapore's professionalism, rule of law and delivery on commitments, and that upholding openness, innovation and people development will keep Singapore a leading global transport hub and trusted decision-making centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What international partners ultimately trust is what Singapore has consistently stood for – professionalism, the rule of law and the ability to deliver on our commitments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As long as we continue to uphold openness and cooperation, pursue relentless innovation, develop our people and move forward hand-in-hand with businesses and workers, I am confident that Singapore will not only maintain its leading position as a global transport hub, but will also become the most trusted decision-making centre for enterprises worldwide, creating more quality jobs for Singaporeans and lay a stronger foundation for the generations to come.

sentences.text: I hope MOT can work together with SG Enable, employers and unions to redesign suitable roles so that more persons with disabilities can participate meaningfully in our transport sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We are actually the world's second most preferred arbitration seat globally, second only to London, and number one in Asia.

sentences.text: Right next door, within sight of our new Tuas Port, the Port of Tanjung Pelapas, backed by global giant APM terminals, is currently expanding.

sections.label: Singapore's survival fundamentals
sections.summary: The passage states that certain fundamentals must never change for Singapore, and asks whether intangible qualities underpinning the system will continue to be tended.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Even the international order is changing before our eyes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But for Singapore, certain fundamentals must never change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Because for Singapore, these are the very conditions for our survival.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The real question is whether we continue tending to the intangible qualities that underpin our system and make us exceptional.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: That, Sir, will determine if we can continue to earn our place in the world.

sections.label: Singapore as decision-making hub
sections.summary: Singapore should aspire to become the place where trade decisions are made with confidence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore should therefore aspire not only to move trade efficiently, but to become the place where those decisions are made with confidence.

sections.label: Trust as economic infrastructure
sections.summary: Trust has become part of Singapore's economic infrastructure, making Tuas Port and Changi T5 investments important.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Trust has become part of Singapore's economic infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: That is why investments in Tuas Port and Changi T5 are so important.

sections.label: Coordinating jobs command higher wages
