sentences.text: The jobs that coordinate regional operations rather than simply execute instructions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These are the jobs that will command higher wages because they create greater value.

sections.label: Singapore as confident decision place
sections.summary: In an uncertain world, Singapore must become the place where transport and supply chain decisions are made with confidence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In a world that is becoming more uncertain, Singapore must become the place where the world's most important transport and supply chain decisions are made with confidence.

sections.label: Workforce transformation and investment returns
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes workforce transformation investments and asks how T5, Tuas Port and transport technology investments will yield better jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Their concern is whether they will be equipped to succeed in this new environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the Government' continued investments in workforce transformation like the OneAviation Manpower Fund and various SkillsFuture initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But my question to the Minister is this: as we invest billions in T5, Tuas Port and new transport technologies, how will the Ministry ensure these investments translate into better jobs, stronger career progression and higher value opportunities for Singaporeans?

sections.label: Strategy for regional transport nerve centre
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry has a long-term strategy to position Singapore as the region's transport and supply chain nerve centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: My question to the Minister is this: beyond strengthening Singapore's physical connectivity, does the Ministry have a long-term strategy to position Singapore as the region's nerve centre for transport and supply chain management?

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: How will MOT work with other agencies and our tripartite partners to anchor these higher-value activities and the good jobs they create in Singapore?

sections.label: Workforce strategy for transport hub
sections.summary: Singapore's human capital strategy must evolve with its infrastructure strategy to remain a global transport hub.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Ports can be built, airports can be expanded, but a future-ready workforce cannot simply be assembled overnight.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: If Singapore is to remain a leading global transport hub over the next two or three decades, our human capital strategy has to evolve with our infrastructure strategy.

sections.label: Integrated National Transport Talent Strategy
sections.summary: A more integrated National Transport Talent Strategy could bring agencies, industries, IHLs and SkillsFuture partners together.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: As we strengthen our position as a global transport hub, we should consider a more integrated National Transport Talent Strategy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Such a strategy could bring together Government agencies, industries, our IHLs and SkillsFuture partners to regularly identify emerging skills, develop future-ready curricula, expand internships and overseas industrial attachments to ensure that Singaporeans are well positioned to take on the high-value jobs that will emerge across our transport sector.

sections.label: Transport sector economic contribution
sections.summary: Transport contributes about a-tenth of GDP and 7% of jobs held by Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Transport is one of the largest economic sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: It contributes about a-tenth of our GDP and 7% of our jobs – good, steady, high-paying jobs, held by Singaporeans who keep people and goods moving, by air, land and sea, every hour, every day.

sections.label: Singapore votes at IMO ICAO
sections.summary: In last year's IMO and ICAO Council elections, Singapore received the highest number of votes in its category.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: In the Council elections for the IMO and for the ICAO last year, Singapore received the highest number of votes in our category.

sections.label: Singapore's global transport agreements
sections.summary: Singapore's agreements help explain flights to over 170 cities and seaport connections to more than 600 locations.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Singapore has built a web of agreements around the world – Air Services Agreements, Green and Digital Shipping Corridors, and many more.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: They help explain why our airport has flights to over 170 cities today and our seaports have connections to more than 600 other locations.

sections.label: Singapore ASEAN Chairmanship opportunity
sections.summary: Next year, as ASEAN Chair, Singapore can advance projects to bring the region closer together.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Next year, when Singapore takes on the ASEAN Chairmanship, we will have the opportunity to advance these projects and more, to bring our region closer together.

sections.label: Global Competitiveness Committee conclusion
sections.summary: The Global Competitiveness Committee, co-chaired with Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling, concluded Singapore must further strengthen its role as a connected global hub.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: The Global Competitiveness Committee, which I co-chaired with Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling, concluded that Singapore must further strengthen our role as a connected global hub.

sections.label: Strategy for host ecosystem
sections.summary: The strategy is not to rely on physical connectivity alone but to build a host ecosystem the industry relies on.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: And that is why our strategy is not to rely on physical connectivity alone.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: It is to build a host ecosystem that the industry is reliant on.

sections.label: Funding and technology examples
sections.summary: Eight hundred million is more than double the funding over the last five years, with examples like automated MRT depots, AI air traffic management and smart port networks.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Eight hundred million is more than double the funding over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: For instance, imagine a fully automated MRT depot that maintains and repairs our trains more efficiently, or an AI-enabled air traffic management system that increases our regional airspace capacity to accommodate the needs of all the airports around us, or a smart port network that makes decisions with shipping lines on how to shift containers on a real-time basis, using tools like digital twins, which Mr Jackson Lam and Ms Tin both spoke about.

sections.label: T5 and Tuas Port capacity
sections.summary: T5 will raise Changi's capacity by more than 50%, and Tuas Port will bring Singapore from 45 million to 65 million TEUs.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: T5 will raise Changi's capacity by more than 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Tuas Port will bring us from 45 million TEUs today to 65 million TEUs in the future.

sections.label: Taxi and private-hire driver numbers
sections.summary: There are over 70,000 taxi and private-hire drivers in Singapore, while all AVs worldwide number around 7,000 cars, under 10% of that population.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Today, there are over 70,000 taxi and private-hire drivers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Even if I gathered every AV around the world today and moved them all to Singapore, that would only be around 7,000 cars – or less than 10% of our total taxi and private-hire car population.

sections.label: Cleaner-energy vehicles and charging points
sections.summary: From 2030 all new car and taxi registrations will be cleaner-energy models, and the Government aims for 60,000 charging points by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: From 2030, all new car and taxi registrations will be cleaner-energy models, supporting Singapore's broader goal for all vehicles to run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government is also working towards deploying 60,000 charging points island-wide by 2030.

sections.label: Heavy vehicle zero emissions incentives
sections.summary: From January 2026, the Heavy Vehicle Zero Emissions Scheme gives $40,000 per newly registered zero-tailpipe-emissions heavy goods vehicle or bus above 3.5 tonnes, and the Electric Heavy Vehicle Charger Grant co-funds up to 50% of charger installation costs, capped at $30,000 per charger for the first 500 chargers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: From January 2026, the Heavy Vehicle Zero Emissions Scheme provides a $40,000 incentive for each newly registered zero-tailpipe-emissions heavy goods vehicle or bus above 3.5 tonnes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Electric Heavy Vehicle Charger Grant also co-funds up to 50% of charger installation costs, capped at $30,000 per charger for the first 500 chargers.

sections.label: Singapore-Kuala Lumpur HSR distance
sections.summary: The roughly 350 kilometre distance between Singapore and Kuala Lumpur is a sweet spot for high-speed rail, widely considered too far to drive conveniently and too short to fly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: At about 350 kilometres in distance between Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, this is a sweet spot for high-speed rail, where it is widely considered to be “too far to drive conveniently and too short to fly”.

sections.label: HSR revival discussions with Malaysia
sections.summary: A reliable 90-minute rail journey would offer an attractive alternative to short-haul flights, easing congestion and supporting both countries' sustainability objectives; Malaysia explored reviving the HSR in 2023 under a different delivery model but no decision has been reached, and Singapore remains open to future discussions should Malaysia bring forward a commercially viable proposal serving b

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: A reliable 90-minute rail journey would offer an attractive alternative to short-haul flights, easing congestion at airports or on highways while supporting both countries' sustainability objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: While Malaysia explored the possibility of reviving the HSR in 2023 under a different delivery model, no decision has since been reached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Singapore Government has consistently maintained that it remains open to future discussions should Malaysia bring forward a commercially viable proposal that serves the interests of both countries.

sections.label: SBS Transit predictive AI maintenance
sections.summary: SBS Transit envisioned predictive AI-enabled maintenance solutions across its bus and rail maintenance operations, consulted workers through the NTUC Company Training Committee initiative before implementing predictive maintenance solutions, and through its Diagnostic Expert Scheme workers could move into higher-value maintenance work with progressive career pathways, enhanced livelihoods and safe

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: To enhance workplace safety and raise productivity, SBS Transit envisioned a predictive AI-enabled maintenance solutions across its bus and rail maintenance operations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Working closely with NTUC through the NTUC Company Training Committee initiative, SBS Transit consulted widely with workers before implementing a suite of predictive maintenance solutions from tyre and track inspections to facility management in its depots and interchanges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Through its Diagnostic Expert Scheme, workers could move into higher-value maintenance work with progressive career pathways, enhanced livelihoods and safer workplaces.

sections.label: P2P drivers' earnings
sections.summary: Unlike salaried employees, P2P drivers stop earning the moment they stop driving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Unlike salaried employees, P2P drivers stop earning the moment they stop driving.

sections.label: AI transition and jobs
sections.summary: This House unanimously passed the Motion on "An AI Transition with No Jobless Growth" in May, and the speaker urges the Government to continue working with NTUC, unions and the Tripartite Jobs Council to identify how jobs are evolving, expand AI Ready SG and encourage more companies to use Company Training Committee grants for job redesign and workforce transformation across the transport sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: This House unanimously passed the Motion on "An AI Transition with No Jobless Growth" in May.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I encourage and urge the Government to continue working closely with NTUC, our unions and our Tripartite Jobs Council to identify how jobs are evolving, expand AI Ready SG to equip more workers with AI capabilities and encourage more companies to leverage our Company Training Committee grants to support job redesign and workforce transformation across the entire transport sector.

sections.label: EV Technical Specialists Skills Pathway
sections.summary: The recently launched Skills Pathway for EV Technical Specialists is an encouraging step in this direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The recently launched Skills Pathway for EV Technical Specialists is an encouraging step in this direction.

sections.label: Sector report card and AVs
sections.summary: A sector-level report card in Industry Transformation Maps could track job creation, quality and the 3Ws, and AVs must complement drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: One possibility is a sector-level report card within our Industry Transformation Maps that tracks whether new and redesigned jobs are being created, whether these jobs are of good quality and whether they deliver what NTUC calls the "3Ws" – better wages, better welfare and better work prospects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Third, AVs must complement our drivers, not compete against them.

sections.label: Redesigning jobs for drivers
sections.summary: Redesigning jobs early, with transition arrangements and drivers at the centre, lets technology bring new skills, roles and a better future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: As long as we redesign jobs for our drivers early, put proper transition arrangements in place and keep our drivers at the centre of that transition, technology can bring them new skills, new roles and a better future.

sections.label: Pathway to better jobs
sections.summary: Livelihoods must be preserved and pathways to the next good job created, so innovation advances together with workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: A pathway to better skills, better jobs and better livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We may not be able to preserve every job exactly as it exists today, but we must preserve livelihoods and create pathways to the next good job.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: If we get this right, Singapore will not only remain as the world's leading transport hub, we will become something even more important – a transport hub where innovation advances together with workers, and where progress is measured not only by how far technology takes us, but by how far it brings our people along.

sections.label: Tuas Port and T5 capacity
sections.summary: Tuas Port will handle 65 million containers a year and T5 will lift Changi towards 140 million passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Tuas Port will handle 65 million containers a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: T5 will lift Changi towards 140 million passengers.

sections.label: Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone
sections.summary: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, signed last year, opens a new chapter for both sides of the Causeway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, signed last year, opens a new chapter for both sides of the Causeway.

sections.label: Changi check-in in Johor
sections.summary: Changi check-in and baggage handling should open in Johor so travellers can begin a Changi journey from Johor Bahru.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, open Changi check-in and baggage handling in Johor itself so a traveller can begin a Changi journey from Johor Bahru.

sections.label: National Crisis Logistics Compact proposal
sections.summary: The Government is urged to set up a National Crisis Logistics Compact with ministries and industry partners, plus stress-tests, an exercise, a statement and a council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If our autonomy is compromised, or even seems to be, we lose the confidence that brings people here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would therefore urge the Government to set up a National Crisis Logistics Compact, bringing MOT, MTI, MFA, the Ministry of Defence and major industry partners into one framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In year one, it should stress-test our five most critical supply chains, run a whole-of-nation logistics exercise modelled after Exercise Northstar, publish a Hub Resilience Statement and establish a standing industry council for crisis coordination.

sections.label: Marine fuel standards role
sections.summary: A country supplying close to a fifth of the world's marine fuel, 56.77 million tonnes last year, should help write those standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A country that supplies close to a fifth of the world's marine fuel, 56.77 million tonnes last year, should be helping write those standards, not receiving them second-hand.

sections.label: Changi and PSA regional gateway
sections.summary: Changi and PSA should be positioned as the trusted gateway for the Johor-Singapore-Riau region, extended to Batam and Bintan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, position Changi and PSA as the trusted gateway for the wider Johor-Singapore-Riau region: off-airport check-in, integrated cross-border transport and bonded cargo corridors, extended to Batam and Bintan, every measure designed to benefit our neighbours as much as ourselves.

sections.label: Three regional connectivity moves
sections.summary: Singapore should develop the Singapore-Johor-Batam-Bintan-Karimun corridor, build a smart sea-air logistics hub and anchor a regional green fuels ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, Singapore should strengthen regional connectivity by developing the Singapore-Johor-Batam-Bintan-Karimun corridor as an integrated economic, logistics and green energy spine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, Singapore should build the world's smartest sea-air logistics hub by applying AI to real operational bottlenecks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And third, Singapore should anchor a regional green fuels ecosystem that creates new opportunities for enterprises, startups and workers.

sections.label: Wider connectivity framework call
sections.summary: The Government is called on to explore a wider Singapore-Johor-Batam-Bintan-Karimun connectivity framework building on the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Transport connectivity can reduce friction, strengthen supply chains, support regional production networks, create jobs and deepen trust among neighbours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I therefore call on the Government to build on the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone by exploring a wider Singapore-Johor-Batam-Bintan-Karimun connectivity framework, supported by interoperable digital systems, trusted data-sharing arrangements and AI-enabled logistics.

sections.label: Singapore maritime hub strengths
sections.summary: Singapore has strengthened its maritime hub position and is now the world's largest transshipment and bunkering hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore has continued to strengthen its maritime hub position through PSA, MPA, bunkering, maritime services, finance, arbitration, logistics, ship management, MRO, digitalisation and green shipping initiative and Singapore is now the world's largest transshipment and bunkering hub.

sections.label: Rising port call costs
sections.summary: Feedback says the cost of calling at Singapore has been rising and some services may be cheaper in ports such as China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We must also address cost and operational bottlenecks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We should take seriously feedback from ship owners and ship suppliers that the cost of calling at Singapore has been rising, and that some services may be cheaper in ports such as China.

sections.label: Reducing port call costs
sections.summary: The port and logistics ecosystem must reduce the total cost of call and movement through shorter turnaround times and other measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our port and logistics ecosystem must therefore reduce the total cost of call and movement through shorter turnaround times, better coordination of bunkering and supplies, digital pre-clearance, AI-enabled scheduling, sufficient heavy vehicle staging and parking capacity and stronger support for marine service and logistics SMEs.

sections.label: Regional clean fuels hub
sections.summary: Singapore should become a trusted regional hub for clean fuels, aggregating feedstock, certifying provenance and emissions, and supporting refining, blending, storage, trading and financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For Singapore, this means becoming a trusted regional hub for clean fuels, aggregating sustainable feedstock, certifying provenance and emissions and supporting refining and blending, storage, trading and financing and supplying aviation and maritime users.

sections.label: Regional green transport strategy
sections.summary: Singapore can become a regional green vessel transformation hub, and the Government is called on to form a coherent regional green transport strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In this way, Singapore can become a regional green vessel transformation hub, connecting fuel supply, bunkering, vessel upgrading, safety standards and skilled jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to bring together our maritime, aviation and clean energy initiatives into a coherent regional green transport strategy, covering sustainable aviation fuel, biofuels, electric harbour craft, methanol and ammonia bunkering and working with our neighbours on common standards, trusted supply chains and regional offtake arrangements.

sections.label: Supporting transport SME capabilities
sections.summary: SMEs can provide specialised capabilities, and the Government is called on to support transport SMEs in building capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As large players invest in green fuel and vessel conversion, SMEs can provide the specialised capabilities that make the ecosystem work – components, sensors, gas detection, emergency response diagnostics, safety equipment and modular training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I therefore call on the Government to support transport SMEs in building capabilities in AI-enabled diagnostics, green fuel safety, alternative-fuel MRO, electrification and maritime compliance.

sections.label: Transport-tech startup partnership strategy
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to develop a transport-tech startup strategy with clearer pathways for startups to partner with SMEs, local enterprises and MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This three-way partnership can help Singapore build a stronger innovation ecosystem around transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I call on the Government to develop a stronger transport-tech startup strategy, with clearer pathways for startups to partner with SMEs, local enterprises and MNCs.

sentences.text: Under the MPA-Singapore Polytechnic Maritime SME Digital Adoption Pilot Programme, SMEs gain knowledge on digital technologies and acquire practical experience in applying automation and data analytics to their operations directly.

sentences.text: Through scholarships, work attachments and mentorship programmes, we will continue to help young Singaporeans gain skills and build meaningful careers in the transport sector.

sentences.text: Our goal is to start with a 1% sustainability aviation fuel uplift, rising to 3% to 5% by 2030, subject to global developments and the wider availability of sustainability aviation fuel.

sections.label: Drones, innovation and economic competitiveness
sections.summary: Drones can improve productivity and safety, and Singapore will support responsible innovation while strengthening long-term economic competitiveness and good jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Many of these use cases improve productivity and worker safety, allowing workers to focus on tasks that call for human judgement and expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are carefully studying how drones can be deployed while being mindful of Singapore's dense urban environment, complex airspace and security needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)

sections.label: Building Singapore's independence
sections.summary: Singapore asserts independence confidently by building strong capabilities, having connection options and deepening international cooperation, not by standing alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: When Singapore builds strong capabilities of our own, when we have options to who we connect with and when we deepen international cooperation so that other countries come to share a genuine stake in our shared success, Singapore will be able to assert our independence with confidence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We do not stay independent by standing alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We stay independent by standing strong enough so that no one else's strategy needs to become ours.

sections.label: Agreement on transport, technology, infrastructure
sections.summary: The House agrees that everyday public transport and global connectivity are not competing priorities, and that people must remain central to what is built.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Attending to the everyday public transport issues and building for Singapore's global connectivity and future are not competing priorities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We agree that the world has grown more uncertain and that Singapore's independence must be built, not assumed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We agree that technology should make us harder to replace, not just harder to keep pace with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We agree that our infrastructure, physical and digital, poured in concrete and written in code, must be built as one so that it can keep pace with a future that will wait for no one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: And we agree that our people must remain at the centre of everything we build.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: When a House this diverse agrees completely on the big one, that is not a coincidence.
